risks.blocker: The 48 V eight-device probe localises the end-of-record high gate: all four A-side SRs (1A, 2A, 3A, 4A) stay at 10.890 V from 247.07 us to the 320 us end, while the final latch conducts only 1.41 A (1.04e-04 A2s per device). The 285.0 A forward peak lands in the release window right after trip, not in the latch. 50 V now has a complete eight-device record only on the cshunt child, and it ends with no gate high, while the stalled base prefix kept B high from 244.47 us. A 1 fF node capacitance is electrically negligible here, so the post-trip gate level is solver-sensitive: neither end state may be quoted as the circuit's behaviour. The 48 V control settles it: its base latches all four A-side gates, while the same 1 fF perturbation latches all four B-side gates (249.38 us, 1.20 A) and leaves A low, with the fault stress moving <0.5 %. The *phase* that holds a gate high in the dead zone is therefore chosen by the numerical trajectory; only the low-current character of the latch (1.2-1.4 A, ~1e-4 A2s per device) survives. The model also implements neither UCC24624 standby turn-off nor thermal/SOA limits, so no side may be declared safely shut down.
risks.next_evidence: Do NOT claim complete shutdown from OC=1V alone. The 48 V eight-SR window is now measured: A-side drive is released at 220.74 us (trip + 5.64 us) and the four A gates re-assert at 247.07 us; the latch carries 1.41 A / 4.16e-04 A2s total, three orders below the 0.0304 A2s forward I2t. Remaining: (a) a solver-independent determination of the dead-state gate state, which the 48 V control shows the model cannot supply (A latches in the base, B in the 1 fF variant; 50 V's prefix and cshunt child disagree as well), and a 50 V eight-device record on a solve that completes without a solver-only aid (the base still stalls at 296.929 us), (b) bench verification of UCC24624 turn-off in the same ~0.1 ms dead state, because the model lacks standby and the gate is reset only by drain reverse bias, and (c) a device SOA/thermal check for the 1.4 A latch and the 285 A release-window peak -- the model has neither. Files: design/v3/power_priority/sr_fault_probe_48v_120a.json, sr_fault_probe_50v_120a_cshunt.json, sr_fault_probe_48v_120a_cshunt.json and hotfault_48v_120a.json.

The 50V 296.928us stall is numerical (smooth 3 V/us dead state, LTE-driven) -- standby cannot close it because tSTBY_DET is 7.5 ms -- and the prefix can support a bounded pre-trip peak discussion but is NOT accepted as full-duration protection validation.  PR #20's documented SOLVER_DIAGNOSTIC is now run: same circuit, trtol 7->1 and abstol 1e-12->1e-13 over 0..220us moves the I(Lr) peak by -0.16 % (-0.163 A), the SR forward peak by +0.002 % and the trip by -81 ns, so the prefix peaks are not a single-solver artifact.  The 48 V control (base run passed the strict log pre-check) moves the same peaks by -0.420 % and -0.411 %: both cases move down under tightening, so the direction is conservative, but the magnitude is sub-percent, not 0.1 %.  The stall now has a solver-aid answer: the cshunt=1 fF child (0 circuit differences) reaches the 320 us stop and moves the same-window peaks by -0.164 % (I(Lr)) / -0.143 % (SR forward) with trip +99 ns; the base itself still stalls, so no number here is hardware evidence.  Closing F01 now also requires an independent engineering waveform review: hotfault_engineering_gate accepts a case only when hotfault_<case>_engineering_review.json is signed and digest-matched to the current deck, log and waveform data, not when the log pre-check passes

ELE-09 ruled out a short-window artifact (22 periods 0.4986 W vs 133 aligned 0.4921 W, sem 0.050 W) and the deck is now exhausted: no un-inventoried dissipative element can hold 0.49 W (Cin ESR 0.61 mW measured, Cbt carries no charge).  Remaining candidates are the port reading (~2 mV of mean Vout) and the behavioral-SR channel/diode split; measured across the four 100 A steps the SR body-diode term moves 118 W/V against the port's 200 W/V, so 1 mV of Vout is worth 0.12 W -- the 0.49 W gap is 2.1 mV, the same order.  The fixed-current legs give 102 W/V as well, so the coupling is to Vout and not to the load current.  Do not relax 0.2 W

the aligned 133-period window confirms the 0.698 W closure is stable (sem 0.050 W); ELE-09's inventory audit leaves only port and numerical candidates, and re-integrating the same samples is falsified (0.80 % within a raw against 86 % across steps).  More step reduction is falsified as well: with the load replaced by a constant-current sink the 0.5 ns leg still settles 15.1 mV above 5 ns and keeps 98.9 % of the resistive 5->0.5 ns endpoint difference, so the four runs sit at different operating points and the model's own V(out) moves with the step.  The sink is faithful (its 5 ns leg matches the resistive one to 0.3 %) but pins the current, not V(out) -- its own window drift is 4.7 mV.  Only a closed V(out) loop can pin the operating point, and that is a different deck; do not relax 0.2 W
